title: Banking System Reform (Separation of Banks) Bill 2018
short_title: Banking System Reform (Separation of Banks) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would separate deposit-taking banking from investment and other financial businesses by restricting banks' activities, ownership links and relationships with non-bank entities.
It would prohibit affiliations with non-banks and investments in specified synthetic products, while generally allowing 24 months to end existing prohibited affiliations, subject to extensions.
The bill would also create parliamentary oversight of the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority and limit Financial Claims Scheme protection to banks complying with activity restrictions.
changes: People working for entities prohibited from affiliating with banks would generally be barred from equivalent positions in banks.
Banks would be prohibited from proprietary trading, market-making and underwriting securities issues.
A joint parliamentary committee would oversee the banking regulator and report on its activities.
Future prudential standards would require parliamentary approval, and either House could disallow a standard.
summary.affected: Banks, their depositors, affiliated non-bank businesses, bank officers and employees, and the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority would be affected.
